 EXHIBIT 99.1
 Exhibit 99.1 
 Sanofi to Acquire Insmed in Strategic Step that Strengthens Long-Term Future
 | 
 ● | 
 Insmed is a transformative acquisition providing strong strategic fit that complements Sanofi’s immunology and rare disease portfolio | ● | 
 Sanofi will gain access to two first-in-disease commercialized products and pipeline assets, strengthening its mid- to long-term growth outlook and its position in
 Respiratory | ● | 
 Sanofi will pay $175 per share, for a total consideration of $41.0 billion (€37.6 billion) in cash. The transaction is expected to be EPS accretive by the end of 2028 | ● | 
 Sanofi retains appropriate capacity to invest in early-stage BD/M&A opportunities. Sanofi confirms its progressive dividend policy and expects to maintain a strong
 credit rating post transaction | 
 BRIDGEWATER, N.J., Nov. 24, 2026 — Sanofi today announced an agreement to acquire Insmed (Nasdaq: INSM), a
 publicly traded, U.S.-based global biopharmaceutical company with two commercialized medicines and a promising, innovative pipeline. The transaction is intended to broaden Sanofi’s presence in respiratory diseases, where significant unmet patient
 need remains. 
 The acquisition includes BRINSUPRI ® 
 (brensocatib) and ARIKAYCE ® (amikacin liposome inhalation suspension), along with a differentiated, phase 3 clinical program, treprostinil palmitil inhalation powder
 (TPIP), which has potential across multiple rare respiratory diseases. The acquisition also brings promising earlier-stage programs and research capabilities across immunology and rare diseases, reinforcing Sanofi’s own innovation and immunology
 capabilities globally. 
 Insmed is a compelling strategic fit, building on Sanofi’s longstanding experience in immunology and rare
 diseases. Combining Insmed’s highly differentiated portfolio and scientific expertise with Sanofi’s global reach is expected to expand patient access to important respiratory medicines while augmenting Sanofi’s commercial leadership and rebuild of
 its pipeline. 
 This acquisition is expected to improve Sanofi’s financial profile over the mid- and long-term and expand the
 company’s portfolio in core focus areas. 
 “I am delighted to welcome Insmed to Sanofi. This acquisition is a major strategic step to significantly
 accelerate our mid- and long-term growth trajectory and further strengthen our mid- and early-stage pipeline,” said Belen Garijo, Chief Executive Officer of Sanofi. “Insmed builds on our already successful presence in respiratory diseases through its
 highly differentiated portfolio, strong science and proven commercial success. Together, we have the opportunity to build on these achievements, reach more patients globally and reinforce our leadership in diseases of significant unmet medical need.
 This acquisition is another example of how we are executing on our strategic roadmap with momentum to drive Sanofi’s next phase of growth.” 
 “The Insmed team has always set out to change what is possible for patients. In just over a year since launch, we
 made BRINSUPRI the standard of care for NCFB patients, while continuing to advance our commercial portfolio and Phase 3 pipeline with a combined multibillion-dollar peak sales potential,” said Will Lewis, Chair and Chief Executive Officer of Insmed.
 “This transaction delivers immediate, certain cash value for Insmed shareholders and ensures the momentum we have built continues. In Sanofi, we have a partner that recognizes the value of our science, commercial execution, and the exceptional
 culture we have created. Together, we expect to bring our therapies to more patients around the world, faster than we ever could on our own.” 
 BRINSUPRI is a small molecule, once-daily, oral, reversible inhibitor of dipeptidyl peptidase 1 (DPP1), approved
 in the U.S., EU, UK and Japan for non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis (NCFB), with the indicated patient populations varying by jurisdiction. BRINSUPRI is the first and only approved treatment for NCFB and a first-in-class DPP1 inhibitor targeting
 neutrophilic inflammation. Following its U.S. launch in August 2025, BRINSUPRI has already reached blockbuster status, delivering $1.09 billion in revenue through September 30, 2026, with substantial additional growth expected. 
 ARIKAYCE is an inhaled antibacterial treatment used in combination with multidrug therapy for certain adults with
 mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) lung disease and is the only approved inhaled therapy specifically indicated for treatment-refractory patients in the U.S., EU and Japan. ARIKAYCE revenues were $433.8 million in 2025, representing 19% annual growth.
 In addition, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in September accepted under priority review an application for ARIKAYCE for the treatment of MAC lung disease as part of a combination antibacterial drug regimen. 
 TPIP is a prostanoid being developed as a once-daily inhaled therapy for pulmonary hypertension and fibrotic lung
 disease. With once-daily dosing and the potential for multiple rare respiratory indications, TPIP could become a significant growth driver for Sanofi beyond 2030, subject to successful clinical development, regulatory approvals, and commercial
 execution. 
 Transaction Terms and Financial Considerations 
 Under the terms of the merger agreement, Sanofi will acquire all outstanding shares of Insmed for $175 per share
 in cash, reflecting a total equity value of approximately $41.0 billion (€37.6 billion). The consideration represents a premium of approximately 46% to Insmed’s unaffected closing share price on November 18, 2026, the day prior to media reports of a
 possible transaction. 
 The transaction is expected to strengthen Sanofi’s mid- to long-term growth profile. The transaction is expected
 to be accretive to Sanofi’s business earnings per share (EPS) by the end of 2028. 
 Sanofi is funding the acquisition through a combination of debt financing and cash on hand, and has secured
 committed financing in support of the transaction. Sanofi will maintain its conservative financial policy. The combined group’s anticipated cash generation is expected to support rapid deleveraging, while retaining flexibility to invest in
 early-stage BD/M&A opportunities. Sanofi remains committed to its capital allocation policy, including its progressive dividend, and expects to maintain a strong credit rating. 
 The transaction has been approved by the boards of directors of both companies. 
 The closing of the transaction is subject to approval by Insmed shareholders, receipt of U.S. and certain
 non-U.S. regulatory approvals and other customary conditions. 
 Subject to the satisfaction or waiver of these conditions, the transaction is expected to close in the first half
 of 2027. 
 The proposed acquisition is not expected to have any impact on Sanofi’s financial guidance for 2026. 
 Advisors 
 Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC is acting as exclusive financial advisor to Insmed, and Freshfields LLP is acting as
 legal advisor to Insmed. Cooley LLP and Hunton Andrews Kurth LLP are also acting as legal advisors to Insmed. Collected Strategies is serving as strategic communications advisor to Insmed. 
 J.P. Morgan is acting as exclusive financial advisor to Sanofi, and Cravath, Swaine & Moore LLP is acting as
 legal advisor to Sanofi. 
 Conference Call for Investors and Analysts 
 Sanofi will host a conference call for investors and analysts at 8:00 a.m. ET today. A presentation will be
 available for download from the Investor Relations section of sanofi.com before the conference call starts. 
 Please register here: 
 https://sanofi.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_utrSGRoUSfSjQtkCADrT_g 
 About BRINSUPRI 
 BRINSUPRI (brensocatib) is a small molecule, once-daily, oral, reversible inhibitor of dipeptidyl peptidase 1
 (DPP1), designed to inhibit the activation of neutrophil serine proteases that are key drivers of chronic airway inflammation in NCFB. 
 In the U.S. and Japan, BRINSUPRI is approved for the treatment of NCFB in adults and pediatric patients aged 12
 years and older. In the EU and UK, it is approved for patients with NCFB aged 12 years and older with two or more exacerbations in the prior 12 months. 
 NCFB is a serious, chronic progressive lung disease in which airways are permanently widened, causing ongoing
 productive cough and exacerbations. Insmed estimates that approximately 500,000 patients in the U.S., 600,000 in France, Germany, Italy, Spain and the UK combined, and 150,000 in Japan are diagnosed with NCFB. These estimates describe diagnosed
 patient populations, and some of these patients in the different jurisdictions are eligible for BRINSUPRI under its current labels. 
 BRINSUPRI is associated with dermatologic adverse reactions, including rash, dry skin and hyperkeratosis, and
 with gingival and periodontal adverse reactions. Patients should be monitored for new skin conditions and receive regular dental care. Live attenuated vaccines should be avoided during treatment. 
 About ARIKAYCE 
 ARIKAYCE (amikacin liposome inhalation suspension) is a novel, inhaled, once-daily liposomal formulation of
 amikacin, approved in the U.S., EU and Japan. 
 In the U.S., it is indicated as part of a combination antibacterial regimen for adults with limited or no
 alternative treatment options who have MAC lung disease and have not achieved negative sputum cultures after at least six consecutive months of a multidrug background regimen. Its U.S. indication was approved under the accelerated approval pathway on
 the basis of sputum culture conversion. Clinical benefit has not yet been established, and continued approval may depend on verification of clinical benefit in confirmatory studies. ARIKAYCE was approved by FDA using the limited population pathway.
 This means FDA has approved this medicine for a limited and specific patient population, and studies on the medicine may have only answered focused questions about its safety and effectiveness. 
 MAC lung disease is a rare and often chronic infection that can cause irreversible lung damage; Insmed estimates
 that 95,000 to 115,000 patients in the U.S. have diagnosed MAC lung disease. These estimates describe diagnosed patient populations, not the populations eligible for ARIKAYCE under its current labels. 
 ARIKAYCE carries a U.S. boxed warning for increased respiratory adverse reactions, including hypersensitivity
 pneumonitis, hemoptysis, bronchospasm and exacerbation of underlying pulmonary disease, which have led to hospitalization in some patients. 
 About TPIP 
 TPIP is a dry powder formulation of treprostinil palmitil, a treprostinil prodrug. It is being developed for
 once-daily administration. Its phase 3 program includes PALM-PAH in pulmonary arterial hypertension, PALM-ILD in pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease, and PALM-PPF in progressive pulmonary fibrosis. A phase 3 study in
 idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is planned to start in the first half of 2027. 
 TPIP is not approved for any indication in any jurisdiction. Its safety and efficacy have not been established. 
 About Sanofi 
 Sanofi is an R&D driven, AI-powered biopharma company committed to improving people’s lives and delivering
 compelling growth. We apply our deep understanding of the immune system to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world, with an innovative pipeline that could benefit millions more. Our team is guided by
 one purpose: we chase the miracles of science to improve people’s lives; this inspires us to drive progress and deliver positive impact for our people and the communities we serve, by addressing the most urgent healthcare, environmental, and societal
 challenges of our time. 
 Sanofi is listed on EURONEXT: SAN and NASDAQ: SNY 
 About Insmed 
 Insmed is a people-first global biopharmaceutical company striving to deliver first- and best-in-class therapies
 to transform the lives of patients facing serious diseases. The Company is advancing a diverse portfolio of approved and mid- to late-stage investigational medicines — including two approved therapies to treat chronic, debilitating lung diseases — as
 well as cutting-edge drug discovery focused on serving patient communities where the need is greatest. Insmed’s commercial portfolio and clinical pipeline are organized around three therapeutic areas: Respiratory, Immunology & Inflammation, and
 Neuro & Other Rare. The Company’s research engine is advancing a wide range of technologies and modalities, including gene therapy, AI-driven protein engineering, RNA end-joining, and synthetic rescue, in the pursuit of future pipeline
 candidates. Headquartered in Bridgewater, New Jersey, Insmed has offices and research locations throughout the United States, Europe, and Japan. Visit www.Insmed.com to learn more or follow us on LinkedIn , Instagram , YouTube ,
 and X . 
 BOXED WARNING AND IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION FOR ARIKAYCE IN THE U.S. 
 WARNING: RISK OF INCREASED RESPIRATORY ADVERSE REACTIONS 
 ARIKAYCE has been associated with an increased risk of respiratory adverse reactions, including hypersensitivity pneumonitis, hemoptysis, bronchospasm, and exacerbation of underlying pulmonary disease that have led to hospitalizations in
 some cases. 
 | 
 Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis has been reported with the use of ARIKAYCE in the
 clinical trials. Hypersensitivity pneumonitis (reported as allergic alveolitis, pneumonitis, interstitial lung disease, allergic reaction to ARIKAYCE) was reported at a higher frequency in patients treated with ARIKAYCE plus background regimen (3.1%)
 compared to patients treated with a background regimen alone (0%). Most patients with hypersensitivity pneumonitis discontinued treatment with ARIKAYCE and received treatment with corticosteroids. If hypersensitivity pneumonitis occurs, discontinue
 ARIKAYCE and manage patients as medically appropriate. 
 Hemoptysis has been reported with the use of ARIKAYCE in the clinical trials.
 Hemoptysis was reported at a higher frequency in patients treated with ARIKAYCE plus background regimen (17.9%) compared to patients treated with a background regimen alone (12.5%). If hemoptysis occurs, manage patients as medically appropriate. 
 Bronchospasm has been reported with the use of ARIKAYCE in the clinical trials.
 Bronchospasm (reported as asthma, bronchial hyperreactivity, bronchospasm, dyspnea, dyspnea exertional, prolonged expiration, throat tightness, wheezing) was reported at a higher frequency in patients treated with ARIKAYCE plus background regimen
 (28.7%) compared to patients treated with a background regimen alone (10.7%). If bronchospasm occurs during the use of ARIKAYCE, treat patients as medically appropriate. 
 Exacerbations of underlying pulmonary disease has been reported with the use of
 ARIKAYCE in the clinical trials. Exacerbations of underlying pulmonary disease (reported as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), infective exacerbation of COPD, infective exacerbation of bronchiectasis) have been reported at a higher
 frequency in patients treated with ARIKAYCE plus background regimen (14.8%) compared to patients treated with background regimen alone (9.8%). If exacerbations of underlying pulmonary disease occur during the use of ARIKAYCE, treat patients as
 medically appropriate. 
 Anaphylaxis and Hypersensitivity Reactions: Serious and potentially
 life-threatening hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported in patients taking ARIKAYCE. Signs and symptoms include acute onset of skin and mucosal tissue hypersensitivity reactions (hives, itching, flushing, swollen
 lips/tongue/uvula), respiratory difficulty (shortness of breath, wheezing, stridor, cough), gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, crampy abdominal pain), and cardiovascular signs and symptoms of anaphylaxis (tachycardia, low blood
 pressure, syncope, incontinence, dizziness). Before therapy with ARIKAYCE is instituted, evaluate for previous hypersensitivity reactions to aminoglycosides. If anaphylaxis or a hypersensitivity reaction occurs, discontinue ARIKAYCE and institute
 appropriate supportive measures. 
 Ototoxicity has been reported with the use of ARIKAYCE in the clinical trials.
 Ototoxicity (including deafness, dizziness, presyncope, tinnitus, and vertigo) were reported with a higher frequency in patients treated with ARIKAYCE plus background regimen (17%) compared to patients treated with background regimen alone (9.8%).
 This was primarily driven by tinnitus (7.6% in ARIKAYCE plus background regimen vs 0.9% in the background regimen alone arm) and dizziness (6.3% in ARIKAYCE plus background regimen vs 2.7% in the background regimen alone arm). Closely monitor
 patients with known or suspected auditory or vestibular dysfunction during treatment with ARIKAYCE. If ototoxicity occurs, manage patients as medically appropriate, including potentially discontinuing ARIKAYCE. 
 Nephrotoxicity was observed during the clinical trials of ARIKAYCE in patients
 with MAC lung disease but not at a higher frequency than background regimen alone. Nephrotoxicity has been associated with the aminoglycosides. Close monitoring of patients with known or suspected renal dysfunction may be needed when prescribing
 ARIKAYCE. 
 Neuromuscular Blockade: Patients with neuromuscular disorders were not enrolled
 in ARIKAYCE clinical trials. Patients with known or suspected neuromuscular disorders, such as myasthenia gravis, should be closely monitored since aminoglycosides may aggravate muscle weakness by blocking the release of acetylcholine at
 neuromuscular junctions. 
 Embryo-Fetal Toxicity: Aminoglycosides can cause fetal harm when administered to
 a pregnant woman. Aminoglycosides, including ARIKAYCE, may be associated with total, irreversible, bilateral congenital deafness in pediatric patients exposed in utero. Patients who use ARIKAYCE during pregnancy, or become pregnant while taking
 ARIKAYCE should be apprised of the potential hazard to the fetus. 
 Contraindications: ARIKAYCE is contraindicated in patients with known
 hypersensitivity to any aminoglycoside. 
 Most Common Adverse Reactions: The most common adverse reactions in Trial 1 at
 an incidence ≥5% for patients using ARIKAYCE plus background regimen compared to patients treated with background regimen alone were dysphonia (47% vs 1%), cough (39% vs 17%), bronchospasm (29% vs 11%), hemoptysis (18% vs 13%), ototoxicity (17% vs
 10%), upper airway irritation (17% vs 2%), musculoskeletal pain (17% vs 8%), fatigue and asthenia (16% vs 10%), exacerbation of underlying pulmonary disease (15% vs 10%), diarrhea (13% vs 5%), nausea (12% vs 4%), pneumonia (10% vs 8%), headache (10%
 vs 5%), pyrexia (7% vs 5%), vomiting (7% vs 4%), rash (6% vs 2%), decreased weight (6% vs 1%), change in sputum (5% vs 1%), and chest discomfort (5% vs 3%). 
 Drug Interactions: Avoid concomitant use of ARIKAYCE with medications associated
 with neurotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, and ototoxicity. Some diuretics can enhance aminoglycoside toxicity by altering aminoglycoside concentrations in serum and tissue. Avoid concomitant use of ARIKAYCE with ethacrynic acid, furosemide, urea, or
 intravenous mannitol. 
 Overdosage: Adverse reactions specifically associated with overdose of ARIKAYCE
 have not been identified. Acute toxicity should be treated with immediate withdrawal of ARIKAYCE, and baseline tests of renal function should be undertaken. Hemodialysis may be helpful in removing amikacin from the body. In all cases of suspected
 overdosage, physicians should contact the Regional Poison Control Center for information about effective treatment. 
 U.S. INDICATION 
 LIMITED POPULATION: ARIKAYCE ® is
 indicated in adults, who have limited or no alternative treatment options, for the treatment of Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) lung disease

 AGREEMENT AND PLAN OF MERGER
 THIS AGREEMENT AND PLAN OF MERGER (this “ Agreement ”) is made and entered into as of November 23, 2026, by and among
 Insmed Incorporated, a Virginia corporation (the “ Company ”), Sanofi, a French société anonyme (“ Parent ”), and Polaris Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware
 corporation and wholly owned Subsidiary of Parent (“ Merger Sub ”) (each of the Company, Parent and Merger Sub, a “ Party ” and, collectively, the “ Parties ”). Certain capitalized terms used in
 this Agreement are defined in Exhibit A .
 RECITALS
 The Parties to this Agreement intend that, upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement, Merger Sub will be merged with and into the Company (the “ Merger ”) in accordance with the VSCA and, if applicable, the DGCL, with the Company continuing as the surviving corporation in the Merger (the “ Surviving Corporation ”),
 whereby (i) each share of Company Common Stock (collectively, the “ Shares ”) issued and outstanding as of immediately prior to the Effective Time (other than Excluded Shares) shall be converted into the
 right to receive the Merger Consideration, in cash, without interest, and subject to any withholding of Taxes, and (ii) the Company shall become a wholly owned Subsidiary of Parent as a result of the Merger.
 The board of directors of the Company (the “ Board of Directors ”) has (i) determined that this Agreement and the Transactions, including the Merger, are in the best
 interest of the Company and its shareholders, (ii) adopted this Agreement and the Plan of Merger attached as Exhibit B (the “ Plan of Merger ”), which constitutes the plan of merger for purposes of Section 13.1-716 of the VSCA, (iii)
 approved the execution, delivery and performance by the Company of this Agreement and the consummation of the Transactions, including the Merger, (iv) directed that this Agreement and the Plan of Merger be submitted to the shareholders of the Company
 for their approval at the Shareholders Meeting and (v) resolved to recommend that the shareholders of the Company approve this Agreement and the Plan of Merger (the “ Company Board Recommendation ”), in
 each case on the terms and subject to the conditions of this Agreement.
 The board of directors of each of Parent and Merger Sub have approved this Agreement and the entry into this Agreement. 
 AGREEMENT 
 The Parties to this Agreement, intending to be legally bound, agree as follows:
 Article I 
 the MERGER 
 1.1 Merger of Merger Sub into the Company . Upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth
 in this Agreement and in accordance with the VSCA and the DGCL, at the Effective Time, the Company and Merger Sub shall consummate the Merger, whereby Merger Sub shall be merged with and into the Company, the separate existence of Merger Sub shall
 cease, and the Company will continue as the Surviving Corporation and a wholly owned Subsidiary of Parent.
 1 
 1.2 Effect of the Merger . The Merger shall have the effects set forth in this Agreement and in the
 applicable provisions of the VSCA and the DGCL. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, at the Effective Time, all of the property, rights, privileges, immunities, powers and franchises of the Company and Merger Sub shall vest in the
 Surviving Corporation, and all of the debts, obligations and liabilities of the Company and Merger Sub shall become the debts, obligations and liabilities of the Surviving Corporation.
 1.3 Closing; Effective Time .
 (a) Unless this Agreement shall have been terminated pursuant to ‎Article VII , the consummation of
 the Merger (the “ Closing ”) shall take place via the electronic exchange of signatures and documents by the Parties on the fourth (4th) business day following the satisfaction or, to the extent permissible
 by applicable Law, waiver of all of the conditions set forth in ‎Article VI (other than those conditions that by their nature are to be satisfied at the Closing, but subject to the satisfaction or, to the extent permissible by applicable Law,
 waiver of those conditions at the Closing), unless another date or place is agreed to in writing by the Company and Parent. The date on which the Closing occurs is referred to in this Agreement as the “ Closing Date ”.
 (b) Subject to the provisions of this Agreement, as soon as practicable on the Closing Date, the Company
 and Merger Sub shall file or cause to be filed (i) articles of merger with the Virginia State Corporation Commission (the “ SCC ”) with respect to the Merger, in such form required by, and executed in
 accordance with, the relevant provisions of the VSCA (the “ Articles of Merger ”), and (ii) a certificate of merger with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware (the “ DE SOS ”) with respect to
 the Merger, in such form required by, and executed in accordance with, the relevant provisions of the DGCL (the “ DE Certificate ”), and the Parties shall take all such further actions as may be required by applicable Law to make the Merger
 effective. The Merger shall become effective upon the issuance of (1) a certificate of merger by the SCC and (2) the filing and acceptance of the DE Certificate with the DE SOS with respect to the Merger, or such other date and time as is agreed upon
 in writing by the Parties and specified in the Articles of Merger and the DE Certificate (such date and time the Merger is effective, the “ Effective Time ”).
 (c) Following the date of this Agreement and prior to the Effective Time, Parent may (subject to the
 immediately following sentence) cause Merger Sub to be re-domiciled as a Virginia corporation governed by the VSCA, in which case the references in Section 1.1 and Section 1.2 of this Agreement to the DGCL and the references in Section
 1.3 of this Agreement to the filings with the DE SOS will no longer apply as the Merger will be governed exclusively by the VSCA by virtue of both the Company and Merger Sub being Virginia corporations. Any election by Parent to effect any such
 re-domiciliation shall (x) be effected in accordance with the applicable provisions of the DGCL and the VSCA and (y) not be effected if it would impair, prevent or materially delay the consummation of the Transactions on the term set forth herein.
 Parent shall provide the Company with drafts of all proposed filings and other documentation to effect such a re-domiciliation, which filings and documentation shall be subject to the prior consent of the Company (not to be unreasonably withheld,
 conditioned or delayed).
 2 
 1.4 Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws; Directors and Officers .
 (a) As of the Effective Time, the articles of incorporation of the Company shall, by virtue of the Merger
 and without any further action, be amended and restated to read in their entirety as set forth on Annex I and, as so amended and restated, shall be the articles of incorporation of the Surviving Corporation until thereafter changed or amended
 as provided therein or by applicable Law, subject to Section ‎5.6(a) .
 (b) As of the Effective Time, the bylaws of the Surviving Corporation shall be amended and restated to
 conform to the bylaws of Merger Sub as in effect immediately prior to the Effective Time, until thereafter changed or amended as provided therein or by applicable Law, subject to Section ‎5.6(a) , except that references to the name of Merger Sub
 shall be replaced by references to the name of the Surviving Corporation.
 (c) As of the Effective Time, (i) the directors of the Surviving Corporation shall be the individuals who
 served as the directors of Merger Sub and (ii) the officers of the Surviving Corporation shall be the individuals who served as the officers of Merger Sub, in each case as of immediately prior to the Effective Time, until their respective successors
 are duly elected and qualified, or their earlier death, resignation or removal. At the Closing, the Company shall use its reasonable best efforts to deliver (or cause to be delivered), executed copies of a customary resignation letter (in form and

 Item 1.01 Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement. 
 Agreement and Plan of Merger 
 On November 23, 2026, Insmed Incorporated (the “ Company ” or “ Insmed ”)
 entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the “ Merger Agreement ”) with Sanofi, a French société anonyme (“ Parent ”), and Polaris Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent (“ Merger
 Sub ”). 
 The Merger Agreement provides that, among other things and on the terms and subject to the conditions of the Merger Agreement, (1) Merger Sub will merge with and into
 the Company (the “ Merger ”), with the Company surviving the Merger as a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent, and (2) at the effective time of the
 Merger (the “ Effective Time ”), each issued and outstanding share of common stock of the Company, par value $0.01 per share (the “ Company Common Stock ”) as of immediately prior to the Effective Time (other than any shares of Company Common Stock that are held by Parent or
 Merger Sub or by any direct or indirect wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, Parent or Merger Sub) will be converted into the right to receive $175.00 in cash, without interest and subject to any withholding of taxes (the “ Merger Consideration ”).
 The Board of Directors of the Company has approved the Merger Agreement and the transactions
 contemplated thereby and resolved to recommend that the Company’s shareholders approve the Merger Agreement and the related plan of merger. 
 Treatment of Company Equity Awards 
 At the Effective Time, (1) each stock option of the Company that is subject only to
 time-based vesting (“ Company Option ”) that is outstanding and unexercised as of immediately prior to the Effective Time, whether vested or unvested, other than any In the Money Converting 2026 Option (as defined below), and that has a
 per share exercise price that is less than the Merger Consideration, will, automatically and without any action on the part of the holder thereof, be canceled and converted into the right to receive an amount in cash (without interest), equal to the
 excess of the Merger Consideration over the per share exercise price of such Company Option, multiplied by the number of shares of Company Common Stock subject to such Company Option as of immediately prior to the Effective Time and (2) each Company
 Option that is unexercised and outstanding as of immediately prior to the Effective Time, whether vested or unvested, and that has a per share exercise price equal to or greater than the Merger Consideration will be canceled for no consideration. 
 At the Effective Time, with respect to each Company Option granted during the 2026 fiscal year that remains unvested as of immediately prior to the Effective Time,
 the portion of such Company Option covering a number of shares equal to 50% of the aggregate number of shares subject to such Company Option as of immediately prior to the Effective Time, which portion will consist of the shares subject to such Company
 Option that are scheduled, in accordance with the vesting schedule in effect on the date of the Merger Agreement, to vest on the latest vesting date or dates following the Effective Time (in reverse chronological order) and that has a per share
 exercise price less than the Merger Consideration (an “ In the Money Converting 2026 Option ”) will, automatically and without any action on the
 part of the holder thereof, be canceled and converted into a cash-based award entitling the holder to receive an amount in cash (without interest) equal to the excess of the Merger Consideration over the per share exercise price of such In the Money
 Converting 2026 Option, multiplied by the number of shares of Company Common Stock subject to such In the Money Converting 2026 Option as of immediately prior to the Effective Time. Each such cash-based award will remain subject to the same terms and
 conditions (including vesting, forfeiture and acceleration provisions) that applied to the corresponding In the Money Converting 2026 Option immediately prior to the Effective Time, except that it will vest and become payable upon the earliest of (1)
 the date the corresponding In the Money Converting 2026 Option would have vested, (2) the date that is six months following the closing date of the Merger and (3) the date the holder is terminated by Parent, the surviving corporation or any of their
 subsidiaries without “cause” or, if such holder is entitled as of the date of the Merger Agreement to accelerated vesting of such award upon a resignation for “good reason,” the date such holder resigns for “good reason.”
 At the Effective Time, each stock option of the Company that is subject to both time-based and performance-based vesting (“ Company PSO ”) that is unvested, unexercised and outstanding as of immediately prior to the Effective Time, other than a Company PSO whose applicable performance-based vesting
 conditions have been satisfied as of immediately prior to the Effective Time, will, automatically and without any action on the part of the holder thereof, be canceled and converted into a cash-based award (a “ Converted PSO ”) entitling the holder to receive an amount in cash (without interest) equal to the excess of the Merger Consideration over the per share exercise price under such
 Company PSO, multiplied by the number of shares of Company Common Stock subject to such Company PSO as of immediately prior to the Effective Time. Each Converted PSO (and the right to payment in respect thereof) will vest and become payable on the date
 the corresponding Company PSO would have vested pursuant to the terms thereof and will be subject to the same terms and conditions (including achievement of applicable performance goals, forfeiture and acceleration provisions) that applied to the
 corresponding Company PSO immediately prior to the Effective Time. Each Company PSO where the applicable performance-based vesting conditions have been satisfied immediately prior to the Effective Time will be canceled and converted into the right to
 receive an amount in cash (without interest) equal to the excess of the Merger Consideration over the per share exercise price of such Company PSO, multiplied by the number of shares of Company Common Stock subject to such Company PSO as of immediately
 prior to the Effective Time.
 At the Effective Time, each restricted stock unit of the Company that is subject only to
 time-based vesting (“ Company RSU ”), whether vested or unvested, other than any Converting 2026 RSUs or any 2027 RSUs (each as defined below), that is outstanding as of immediately prior to the Effective Time will, automatically and
 without any action on the part of the holder thereof, be canceled and converted into the right to receive an amount in cash (without interest) equal to the number of shares of Company Common Stock subject to such Company RSU as of immediately prior
 to the Effective Time, multiplied by the Merger Consideration. 
 At the Effective Time, with respect to each Company RSU granted during the 2026 fiscal year (other than any Company RSU granted to a non-employee member of the Board
 of Directors of the Company) that remains unvested as of immediately prior to the Effective Time, the portion of such Company RSU covering a number of shares equal to 50% of the aggregate number of shares subject to such Company RSU as of immediately
 prior to the Effective Time, which portion will consist of the shares subject to such Company RSU that are scheduled, in accordance with the vesting schedule in effect on the date of the Merger Agreement, to vest on the latest vesting date or dates
 following the Effective Time (in reverse chronological order) (a “ Converting 2026 RSU ”) will, automatically and without any action on the part
 of the holder thereof, be canceled and converted into a cash-based award entitling the holder to receive an amount in cash (without interest) equal to the Merger Consideration multiplied by the number of shares of Company Common Stock subject to such
 Converting 2026 RSU as of immediately prior to the Effective Time. Each such cash-based award will remain subject to the same terms and conditions (including vesting, forfeiture and acceleration provisions) that applied to the corresponding Converting
 2026 RSU immediately prior to the Effective Time, except that it will vest and become payable upon the earliest of (1) the date the corresponding Converting 2026 RSU would have vested, (2) the date that is six months following the closing date of the
 Merger and (3) the date the holder is terminated by Parent, the surviving corporation or any of their subsidiaries without “cause” or, if such holder is entitled as of the date of the Merger Agreement to accelerated vesting of such award upon a
 resignation for “good reason,” the date such holder resigns for “good reason.”
 At the Effective Time, each Company RSU granted during the 2027 fiscal year (other than any
 Company RSU granted to a non-employee member of the Board of Directors of the Company) that is outstanding and unvested as of immediately prior to the Effective Time (a “ 2027 RSU ”) will, automatically and without any action on the part
 of the holder thereof, be canceled and converted into a cash-based award entitling the holder to receive an amount in cash (without interest), equal to the Merger Consideration multiplied by the number of shares of Company Common Stock subject to
 such 2027 RSU as of immediately prior to the Effective Time. Each such cash-based award will remain subject to the same terms and conditions (including vesting, forfeiture, settlement, acceleration provisions, and payment schedules) that applied to
 the corresponding 2027 RSU immediately prior to the Effective Time. 
 At the Effective Time, each performance-based restricted stock unit of the Company (“ Company
 PSU ”), whether vested or unvested, that is outstanding as of immediately prior to the Effective Time will, automatically and without any action on the part of the holder thereof, be canceled and converted into the right to receive an
 amount in cash (without interest), equal to the Merger Consideration multiplied by the number of shares of Company Common Stock subject to such Company PSU as of immediately prior to the Effective Time (with any performance-based conditions
 applicable to any portion of such Company PSU with a performance period that has not been completed as of such time deemed achieved at maximum performance). 
 Conditions to the Merger 
 The completion of the Merger is subject to the satisfaction or waiver of certain customary mutual closing conditions, including (1) the approval of the Merger
 Agreement and the related plan of merger by the affirmative vote of more than two-thirds of all the votes entitled to be cast by the holders of the outstanding shares of Company Common Stock (the “ Company Shareholder Approval ”), (2) the expiration or termination of the applicable waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended, and the receipt of
 certain foreign antitrust and foreign direct investment clearances and (3) the absence of any law or order by a court or other governmental entity of competent jurisdiction prohibiting or making illegal the consummation of the Merger. The obligation of
 each party to consummate the Merger is also conditioned on the other party’s representations and warranties being true and correct (subject to certain customary materiality exceptions) and the other party having performed in all material respects its
 obligations under the Merger Agreement, and the obligation of Parent and Merger Sub to consummate the Merger is additionally conditioned on no material adverse effect on the Company having occurred since the execution of the Merger Agreement. The
 consummation of the Merger is not subject to any financing condition.
 Termination 
 The Merger Agreement contains termination rights for each of the Company and Parent, including, among others, (1) if the consummation of the Merger does not occur on
 or before 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on August 23, 2027 (subject to automatic extension to 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on November 23, 2027 and further automatic extension to 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on February 23, 2028, in each case, under specified
 circumstances), (2) if the Company Shareholder Approval is not obtained at the meeting of the Company’s shareholders held for purposes of obtaining such Company Shareholder Approval (or any adjournment thereof), and (3) subject to certain conditions
 and prior to receipt of the Company Shareholder Approval, (a) by Parent if the Board of Directors of the Company changes its recommendation in favor of the Merger or (b) by the Company if the Company wishes to terminate the Merger Agreement to
 substantially concurrently enter into a definitive agreement providing for a Superior Proposal (as defined by the Merger Agreement). The Company and Parent may also terminate the Merger Agreement by mutual written consent.
 The Company is required to pay Parent or its designee a termination fee of $1,125,000,000 in cash on termination of the Merger Agreement under specified
 circumstances, including, among others, termination by Parent in the event that the Board of Directors of the Company changes its recommendation in favor of the Merger or termination by the Company to enter into an agreement providing for a Superior
 Proposal. The Merger Agreement also provides that the parties may seek to compel the other parties to specifically perform its obligations under the Merger Agreement.
 Financing 
 Parent has obtained debt financing commitments for the purpose of financing the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement. Parent’s debt commitments to
 finance in part the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement include bridge facilities on the terms set forth in a bridge facilities mandate letter. The obligations of the lenders to provide debt financing under the bridge facilities mandate
 letter are subject to the satisfaction (or waiver) of the conditions set forth in the bridge facilities mandate letter.
 Pursuant to the Merger Agreement, the Company is required to, and to cause its subsidiaries to, use commercially reasonable efforts to provide Parent with customary
 cooperation in connection with the debt financing, subject to certain limitations.
 Other Terms of the Merger Agreement 
 The Merger Agreement contains customary representations and warranties of the Company,
 Parent and Merger Sub, in each case generally subject to customary materiality qualifiers. Additionally, the Merger Agreement provides for customary pre-closing covenants of the Company, Parent and Merger Sub, including covenants relating to the
 Company using commercially reasonable efforts to conduct its and its subsidiaries’ business in the ordinary course in all material respects and refraining from taking certain actions without Parent’s consent, subject to certain exceptions. The
 Company, Parent and Merger Sub also agreed to use their respective reasonable best efforts to cause the Merger to be consummated. 
 The Merger Agreement provides that, during the period from the date of the Merger Agreement until the earlier of the Effective Time and the valid termination of the
 Merger Agreement, the Company will be subject to certain restrictions on its ability to solicit certain alternative acquisition proposals from third parties, provide non-public information to third parties and engage in discussions or enter into
 agreements with third parties regarding certain alternative acquisition proposals, subject to customary exceptions.
